Scorecard

Every claim about the Indus script, on one scale

Published keys, meaning claims and our own findings, each given one tier by two raters working blind under a rubric sealed before rating. Nothing has reached the top two tiers yet.

65Claims

The tiers

Each claim gets the first tier that applies, from the top. The two raters agreed well: Cohen’s kappa 0.84 over 65 claims, against a bar of 0.8 set in advance. A third rater settled the 8 rows they split on, and those are marked “split”.

  • Anchored
    0
    An outside anchor (a bilingual, or a read script) confirms it on data not used to make it.
  • Predicted forward
    0
    A sealed prediction, made before the data were seen, came true.
  • Survives refutation
    10
    Passed a pre-registered or held-out test that could have refuted it.
  • Refuted
    7
    Its own prediction failed a test with enough power, or its numbers fail on rerun.
  • Can’t test yet
    27
    Stated precisely and the data are held, but no test we can run is strong enough.
  • Pending
    4
    Testable on data in hand, or seen only in exploration; not yet decided.
  • Can’t be benched
    17
    Not stated sign by sign or as a rule, or the key or paper is not available.

What our tests can and cannot see

  • Fitting a dictionary can count against a key that covers every sign at Indus text length. It can never count for one: keys fitted to random sign strings score higher than the true Linear B key (lb_shape_ladder).
  • A sign tied to a seal’s animal is visible only if it covers an extra 20% or more of the non-unicorn seals (shorthorn bull: 20%; elephant: 40%). Weaker ties can be neither confirmed nor ruled out (animal_tie_power).
  • Tablets quoting seals from their own city cannot be seen at Indus text size: a real case from Ur III was caught in only 31% of trials (tablet_quoting).

All claims

Calibration: a known script scored as if it were an Indus claim2 claims
  • Ventris (true Linear B key): The true Linear B sign-to-sound key, scored as if it were an Indus claim at Indus text shape
    Survives refutation
    experiments/lb_shape_ladder/RESULTS.md: in a sealed test that could have refuted it (the same key fails 0/20 on scrambled text and 13/20 at 74% coverage), the true key beats its shape-keeping shuffles in 20/20 held-out subsamples at R1 (0.204 vs 99th pct 0.182); certify fails (0/20), but S does not require certification. · split (S/U/S)
  • keys fitted to random sign strings: Keys hill-climbed to fit noise, scored the same way
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/yj_ic_refute/RESULTS.md: keys fitted to shuffled text beat their own shuffles by construction (IC 0.43, p = 0.001, ‘a pass would have meant nothing’), and lb_shape_ladder shows they outscore the true key (0.254 vs 0.204 at R1), so no held test can tell them from a real key. · split (S/U/U)
Published sound keys6 claims
  • Pierson (glossa-lab): Partial phonetic readings (605 readings)
    Refuted
    experiments/bench_pierson/RESULTS.md: the author’s own validation fails on rerun (92.8% coverage identical on a token-shuffled corpus; ‘Uniform 0.0%' is a case artefact, fair baseline 49% vs 55%; M77 replication 70.5% reruns as 58.7%/54.7%), though the bench’s own power gate failed so the readings themselves are only untestable by fit.
  • Yajnadevam (2024): Full Sanskrit sign-to-sound key; the corpus reads as Vedic Sanskrit
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/yj_ic_refute/RESULTS.md: key does not beat its shuffles (p 0.22-0.27) but at the real corpus’s null width planted power is only 5/20 or 2/20 (10-25%), sealed verdict ‘untestable with this lexicon’.
  • Fairservis (1992): Dravidian readings of signs as names and honorifics
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/yj_ic_refute/RESULTS.md states ‘Fairservis and Rao tables are not held’, and atlas 1.1’s earlier ‘null’ rests on the CPW fit score that lb_certify shows cannot refute (true LB key 2.258 vs shuffled 99th 2.301).
  • S. R. Rao: Indo-Aryan syllabic values
    Can’t be benched
    docs/NEGATIVE_ATLAS.md 1.1 reports only ‘Fairservis and Rao: null’ on a fit score later downgraded to ‘unsupported’, and yj_ic_refute/RESULTS.md says the Rao table is not held.
  • S. Kalyanaraman: Rebus readings (Meluhha metalwork lexicon)
    Can’t be benched
    docs/outreach/REPLIES.md: he sent about 12 rows of meanings with only about 6 Mahadevan numbers and no sound values, below the sealed gate of 15 M-numbers with sound values in docs/prereg/kalyanaraman_key.md; the full table has not arrived.
  • Adelman (2026): Convergent Dravidian key, ‘systemic coherence to the rarest sign’
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/bench2026/RESULTS.md: full text behind a login (HTTP 403), no public sign-value table, ‘Adelman Dravidian key beats chance: Untestable (no public table)'.
What the texts are for2 claims
  • Kriger & Hunt (2026): Seal texts are registration codes (uniqueness, edge pattern, numerals, near-duplicates)
    Refuted
    experiments/bench2026/RESULTS.md (pre-registered): their uniqueness claim reverses on rerun (88.2% vs nulls 97.5-99.2%, below every draw), numerals not penultimate (p = 0.46), ‘digit 2’ is the M99 connective (27.7% without it); only the non-diagnostic edge pattern replicates.
  • Raghavendra (2026, SIGIL): A sound-free emblem system reproduces the Indus statistics
    Can’t test yet
    Claim is precise and the data are held, but the sealed held-out fit test failed its kill gate (98/100 planted SIGIL corpora rejected, about 40-45% unparsed at Indus size), so no test on held data can tell the claim from noise; the 6-criteria match is the claimant’s own in-sample result, not a held-out pass. · re-rated after a new sealed test (was Pending)
What signs mean (44 published proposals)44 claims
  • Wells (2015): fish + number clusters as fixed units
    Survives refutation
    README.md #5: six + fish is a fixed expression on clean held-out data (7 of 10 vs 3% base, q~6e-8) and atlas 6.9 says the effect survives (29/40) though carried by M59; Parpola’s seven + fish has no support.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2023): standardized-capacity vessel; on tablet reverses it gives one of four licence-fee slabs
    Refuted
    Central predictions (N tracks quantity, find-spot clustering, obverse x tier) failed at power 0.985-0.99 (m328_measure Q1-Q3, tablet_archives p 0.75 power 0.96); the phase-drift cell in r_symmetry tests a different thing, not the claim’s find-spot prediction. · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Refuted)
  • Mukhopadhyay (2023): obverse = licensed activity; reverse = fee slab for that activity
    Refuted
    Obverse texts do not split by fee tier (S 101, p 0.75, power 0.96), and the null holds on M77 Harappa (p 0.79, power 0.92). · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Refuted)
  • Mukhopadhyay (2023): seal animals are emblems of guilds or tax authorities; same-emblem seals share licence content
    Refuted
    Unicorn vs other AUC 0.52 at null, same-emblem Jaccard null in 16/16, holds on ICIT square seals (AUC 0.523, power 1.00). · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Refuted)
  • Mukhopadhyay (2019): metrological units of volume
    Refuted
    Sealed signmap test: pooled stroked jars 0.74x on pottery vs 2x predicted, power 0.96, kill met; rests on ICIT alone (M77 power 0.65), M345 2.0x only exploratory. · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Pending)
  • Kenoyer & Meadow; Rao (2010; 2018): transaction tokens or ration records; deliberate disposal of tablet groups
    Refuted
    0/5 pre-registered tablet-archive tests pass; deposit test null at power 0.98 and holds on M77 (T1 p 0.84, power 1.00); only the multiplicity test was underpowered. · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Refuted)
  • Mukhopadhyay (2025 (SSRN 5079207; earlier 2023 SSRN 4412558)): fish signs denote gemstones, beads, jewellery and shiny metals (Dravidian min/mani; Mesopotamian ‘fish-eye stones’ NA4.IGI.KU6)
    Can’t test yet
    The claim has an operational prediction (fish enriched on bead/jeweller-unit objects) and the units are coded, but experiments/bead_workshops/RESULTS.md gives only 32 primary objects in 4 units, with clustered power of 0.21 at 1.5x and 0.56 at 2x, so no test was run; the meluhha West-objects side (W220 fish 6 vs 3.09 expected, p = 0.07) is also low-powered and not decisive. · re-rated after a stale catalogue entry was fixed (was Pending)
  • Mukhopadhyay (2022 (SSRN 4110151)): ‘gold’ and ‘ratti’ (seed weight) signs; fish-like signs = gemstones and weight standards
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: only 18 implement texts and 5 gold/silver objects (n <= 5), and the claim is built on those same objects, so no independent sample exists.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2023): a denomination of a volumetric unit stamped on pointed-base goblets
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: the needed goblet capacities per stamp type are not in open data and every known example is the basis of the claim, so no test is possible on held data.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2023): texts encode no personal names or place names; they encode commodities, fees and rules
    Can’t test yet
    The central contrast, names versus commodity/fee texts, is undecidable: identifiers/RESULTS.md matches neither the identifier model nor the label model, and administration P13 finds 0/12 commodity signs with no stated power; only the toponym half survived a powered test (toponyms T2a, power 0.83). · split (S/U/U)
  • Mukhopadhyay; Kharakwal et al. (2023; 2012): an occupation (agate workers?) needing gate passes at fortified Kanmer
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: Kanmer has 4 distinct ICIT texts (n = 4), far below any usable power.
  • Mukhopadhyay; Kharakwal et al. (2023; 2012): emblem of a Kutch authority (wild ass is a Kutch animal)
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: Kutch sites outside Dholavira hold 19 distinct texts in all (power < 20 texts) and the sign is not a regular sign-list entry.
  • Mukhopadhyay; Kenoyer (2019; 2006): crop/commodity; with numerals on jar bodies it gives a quantity of grain or oil
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: vessel form recorded for about 20 of 650 inscribed vessels (power near zero), and the Lothal-back test (administration t4, W390 p = 0.65) has no stated power.
  • Mahadevan (2009): one who carries a sacrificial vessel (priestly officiant); jar = priestly elite (Agastya, ‘jar-born’)
    Can’t test yet
    The claim’s sign, the jar-bearer ligature, was never tested; the powered null (reg_harappa: M342 by big square, p = 0.54, power 1.0 at 3x) covers only the bare jar sign at Harappa, and administration notes that the citadel samples ‘can exclude only large effects’, so the priest-precinct prediction has no powered test. · split (R/U/U)
  • Mahadevan (2009): warrior (‘one who carries the arrow’)
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/administration/RESULTS.md P6 (final M211 on Harappa F, p = 0.50/0.43) gives no power figure, and experiments/dominik_w090 held-out is ‘untestable (power 0.24 at n = 8)'.
  • Mahadevan (via Jyothibabu review) (1980s-2009): officer title (Tamil kaviti ‘yoke-bearer’); later Sanskrit bhartr ‘lord’
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: a title needs an external role record not held; only positional (L1) behaviour can be measured, which cannot tell a title reading from other readings.
  • Parpola (1994; 2010): M87 = vel (spear/god); fills the same slot as fish (M-172 vs H-6)
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/parpola_rules34/RESULTS.md: the pre-registered known-answer gate detected 1/50 = 2% of planted substitutions (bar 80%), so the non-passing real pair (dev p 0.22, held-out 0.31, new sites 0.23) can neither confirm nor refute the claim at this corpus size. · re-rated after a stale catalogue entry was fixed (was Pending)
  • Parpola (1994; 2010): fixed names of the god Murukan
    Can’t test yet
    The powered prereg pair test (gate 96%) confirms only Parpola’s starting observation, M403 -> M87, on held-out data and new sites. It cannot tell ‘Muruka-vel’ from ‘M403 + numeral 2’, and calibration on Linear B finds this form underpowered (AUC 0.67, no verdict on 27 of 30 true claims). Split: the squirrel half is absent (0 of 74), which a powered gate would have seen. · re-rated after its test was calibrated on a script we can read (was Pending)
  • Parpola (cited by Mukhopadhyay 2023) (1975): the ancient name of Chanhu-daro
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/toponyms/RESULTS.md finding 4: M93’s locality (10/10 texts, splits 2/2 and 3/3) only re-splits the corpus the claim came from, and the test that separates a place name from a scribal habit, travel on sealings, cannot run because ‘almost no Chanhu-daro sealings survive’. · split (S/U/U)
  • Parpola (sign list, as reproduced on Wikiversity) (1994): weight / metrology
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/weight_sign/RESULTS.md maps Parpola 193 to M206/M208, which occur in only 9 distinct texts (1 fresh, gate power 0.005). The M197 fallback has 5 fresh texts with planted power 0.068 against the 0.8 bar, and its seen-data signal (p 0.0014) is exploratory, with a failed negative control. · re-rated after a stale catalogue entry was fixed (was Pending)
  • Parpola (sign list) (1994): porter/carrier; Dravidian homophones include ‘lever of a steelyard’
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/assemblage/RESULTS.md: WEIGHT units not enriched but planted power at 3x is 0.00-0.035, and the M1 storage signal was one seal.
  • Wells (as reported by Rao 2018) (2015): volumetric measure of about 40 L; a related sign about 160 L
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/m342_offsite/RESULTS.md: the pre-registered vessel test is untestable (power 0.465, about 250 pottery texts needed); with no vessel capacities held, the ~40 L prediction has no powered test, and m328_measure’s tablet-size, batch and locus nulls (power 0.98) test a count reading, not pot volume. · split (U/R/U)
  • Kenoyer (2006 (cited in Mukhopadhyay 2019)): measure of oil or grain in the jar before sealing
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/magnitude/RESULTS.md: 0 inscribed vessels have a recorded capacity, so stroke count vs capacity cannot be tested on held data.
  • Kenoyer (2020): pre-Mature post-firing pot marks: owner or user marks that became script signs
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/potters_marks/RESULTS.md: M342/M347 do have pre-Mature graffiti ancestors, but the frame-vs-core test is inconclusive (OR 1.26, p = 0.39) with power 0.33 at 2x.
  • Halim & Vidale; Kenoyer (1984; 1990s): stoneware-bangle inscriptions are workshop, batch or owner marks
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/bangle_oval/RESULTS.md: H1 untestable (n = 0 new bangles, ~19 needed for 0.8) and the workshop descriptive (5/27 vs 0/13, p = 0.15) has power <= 14%.
  • Frenez & Tosi; Frenez (2005; 2018): seals controlled access to stored goods; elephant-seal boxes tied to maritime trade
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/sealing_function/RESULTS.md: door-peg test power 0.004-0.012, ‘closed by sample size, not by evidence’; administration P13-P14 nulls carry no power figure.
  • Laursen (2010): a prefix common on Gulf-type seals; part of a non-Harappan (Dilmun) language or name formula
    Can’t test yet
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: only 3 Gulf texts carry W032, ‘power negligible unless the mapping adds more’.
  • Laursen; Parpola (2010; 1994): Gulf seals write another language with Indus signs
    Can’t test yet
    The claimant’s observable (Gulf round seals break Indus order) holds, but it also fits a round-seal genre or pseudo-writing, and the data cannot separate the three readings; round_own_order (power 0.995) refutes only a derived ‘own grammar’ version on a mixed set of 32 (10 home), with a Gulf-only subgroup too small to test, so this is not R. · split (R/U/U) · re-rated after its test was re-run under other sign lists and the other edition (was Refuted)
  • Farmer, Sproat & Witzel (2004): non-linguistic emblems of deities, clans and offices (cf. kudurru symbols); number signs symbolic
    Can’t test yet
    docs/NEGATIVE_ATLAS.md 3.1-3.2: language vs code is untestable (classifier gate failed, balanced accuracy 0.69 vs 0.80 bar), and the emblem-text null (context Q1) has no power calibration.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2025): string of beads; with fish on the Kalibangan drain pipe it labels a bead container
    Pending
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: testable but not run; sign identity still to be fixed from the paper’s figures, power unknown.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2019): members of a class are mutually exclusive logograms (a paradigm: one slot, one filler)
    Pending
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: testable on M77 dev/held-out (crop group 301 texts) but her counts ‘were never put under a null’; not run.
  • Mukhopadhyay (2021): Indus word pilu ‘elephant/ivory/toothbrush tree’, borrowed as Akkadian piru
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: a language claim with no sign attached, so no script test follows.
  • Mahadevan (c. 2011): UNVERIFIED: ties the fish sign to the Great Bath ritual
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: marked UNVERIFIED, full text not reached, so the claim is not held in operational form.
  • Parpola (1994; 2010): vata-min ‘north star’
    Can’t be benched
    Not stated sign by sign: Parpola’s fig sign has no number or drawing held, and two blind shape mappers disagreed (M326 vs M325, both low), so the fig+fish pair cannot be fixed or counted. · re-rated after a new sealed test (was Pending)
  • Wells (2015): 17 signs identified with Dravidian values; some sequences are verbs or nouns
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: book not open, the 17-sign list was not reached.
  • Vidale (2004-2005): bison emblem marks clans in the western trade
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv row VID05-bison-abroad: ‘Not a sign claim’, and ‘marks clans’ has no operational prediction; the cited context Q1 and Meluhha tests do not test it. · split (U/N/N)
  • Possehl (1996): no new sign meaning; surveys earlier decipherments; seals as identity/office markers
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: ‘No sign-level claim to test’.
  • Koskenniemi (with Parpola) (1970s-1981): no meaning claims found; segmentation and sign classes only
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: no meaning claims found, segmentation and sign classes only, so nothing stated sign by sign as a reading.
  • Fairservis (1992): fish = loom-twist, used as an honorific; seal texts = names and titles of chiefs
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: book text not read, and experiments/literature/RESULTS.md says his specific values are UNVERIFIED; the earlier shuffle-bench null is a fit score that lb_certify shows cannot refute.
  • Kalyanaraman (2010-2019): rebus readings for metalwork and ‘wealth-accounting ledgers’ (e.g. drongo = steel)
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: no fixed one-value-per-sign key, so any outcome fits (REPLIES.md: meanings only, about 6 numbered rows).
  • Knorozov, Volchok et al. (1965-1981): Dravidian values for many signs (specific values not reached)
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: ‘Values not in hand’.
  • Kinnier Wilson (1974): Sumerian logogram values
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: ‘Sign values not in hand’; the Sumerian-language test (atlas 1.8, z 0.33-0.54) is itself untestable at planted z 0.3-2.8.
  • Laursen & Steinkeller; Parpola; others (1977-2017): Meluhha goods in cuneiform (carnelian, ivory, ab-ba and mes wood, copper, gold dust, dar-bird, dogs) as possible sign referents
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: ‘No published scholarly sign-to-good link was found’, so the claim names no signs; the project’s own candidates (meluhha goods: 0 of 4 enriched on 30 objects) were tested without stated power.
  • Green; Mukhopadhyay (2018-2023): seals and weights co-occur in public buildings (Mohenjo-daro DK-G 8A, 6A) used for administration
    Can’t be benched
    experiments/meaning_claims/CATALOGUE.csv: ‘Not a sign claim’; it concerns co-location of seals and weights in buildings, not a script reading.

Only the Murukan row has had its test checked on a script we can read (Linear B): there the test never passed a made-up claim but gave no answer on most true ones. The other meaning rows are not calibrated.

Our own findings11 claims
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #1
    Survives refutation
    README.md #1: on a clean held-out split real order beats permutations in 40% of 321 runs vs 5.7% chance (q~8e-72), red-teamed; codes pass the same test, so it shows sequential structure only.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #3
    Survives refutation
    README.md #3: clean held-out 11/19 ticked fish final vs 7% for plain fish (p = 0.004) and red team #31 finds it again at post-1977 sites (4 of 6, p = 0.02-0.04); split: q = 0.54 across all tests and it misses 0.05 when fish are lumped.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #4
    Survives refutation
    experiments/context/RESULTS.md Q4: foreign round seals +2.17 bits/sign (planted shuffled-order detection 0.99), replicated on M77 West Asian finds (+1.96, p = 1e-4); split: the ‘square abroad / not format’ part was corrected (home round seals break order too).
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #5
    Survives refutation
    README.md #5: six + fish fixed on clean held-out data, 7 of 10 vs 3% base (q~6e-8), replicated in Wells 13 of 33.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #6
    Survives refutation
    README.md #6: object-type vocabulary on clean held-out data, AUC copper 0.87 to sealing 0.67, all above permutation 95th pct 0.55-0.61.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #9
    Survives refutation
    README.md #9: positional classes parse 76% of unseen texts vs 44% for shuffles and 77% at sites absent from M77; split: the specific 11 roles are only weakly supported (p = 0.013, q = 0.085).
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #10
    Survives refutation
    README.md #10: pair order replicates on held-out (115/138 follow dev order, p = 3e-16) and core_semantics prereg passed 8/9; split: typology formal verdict inconclusive (4/5) and it passes only 3-9 of 10 noise runs.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #11
    Survives refutation
    README.md #11: the fish family substitutes as a set on held-out data, p = 0.0002-0.0004 (core_semantics); Parpola’s fish = deity reading failed held-out.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #7
    Can’t test yet
    README.md #7: the 31/34 result depends on direction labels; under ICIT labels 19/23 just misses the bar, red team ICIT 15/22 (p = 0.07), and only 4-8 lines are labelled alike in both editions, ‘too few to test’.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #2
    Pending
    README.md #2: inventory comparison is ‘Descriptive comparison, not a hypothesis test’ (120 signs cover 90% of tokens), with no sealed or held-out test.
  • this project: README ‘What we can defend’ row #8
    Pending
    README.md #8 is marked exploratory: same legend -> same sign face 8/8 is an ‘all-data test, not held out’.
